red_flags.detail: Five of Wave 2's seven gate-refusals were exactly this class inside the arc's own machinery: a fabricated negative control (W2-149), unfalsifiable verdict logic that could never emit UNRESOLVED (W2-270), tautological/vacuous invariant theater (W2-119), a hand-read-off-the-paper patch proposal with 4 of 6 tiers wrong (W2-188), and comment-only diagnostics standing in for enforced checks (W2-150r). All are named and carried by the arc's own FINDINGS_WAVE2.md, and the first three were independently re-verified as fixed in Wave 3 (read directly: W3-149r, W3-017/W4-017r chain).

Cell W2-270's own directory is internally inconsistent: output.txt (identical to output.txt.orig_claim) reports a run terminated early at depth 8 with VERDICT: UNRESOLVED, but the (non-orig_claim) results.json in the same directory contains a full depth-7-through-11 run with a different verdict (RESOLVED-B, achieved_digits=1) that is never mentioned in FINDINGS_WAVE2/3/4.md — the arc's actual closure of this question is instead credited to the separate cell W4-270r (read directly, self-consistent). The stray results.json looks like an orphaned/superseded artifact that was never reconciled with its own cell's output.txt or cited anywhere.

The W4-270r/W2-270 gap-slope observable is explicitly declared to have no closed-form perturbative expression in the banked machinery; the arc's own gate (G8) states the achieved precision (1-2 honest digits) is roughly 4x-7x short of the sealed >=15-digit PSLQ floor, so the 'RESOLVED-B' verdict is a bounded-negative on a purely numeric route, not an exact identification -- correctly labeled as such in-cell, but worth flagging since the census delta counts it as a closure (CLOSED) alongside genuinely exact results in the same wave tables.

arc_verdict.json's one-line claim only narrates Wave 1's headline (e3, L39, D4 ceiling, two refutations) even though the same directory and verdict file cover Waves 2-5, which contain their own separate closures, refutations, and several corrections of earlier waves' agent-overclaims (W2-149->W3-149r, W3-017->W4-017r->W5-017r, W2-270 lineage). arcs.seat_note: This is a large, well-instrumented mechanical closure batch (65 cells, 5 waves) whose main asset is methodological: its adversarial-verification layer visibly catches and names real agent-overclaim failures (fabricated controls, unfalsifiable verdict logic, hand-read errors) inside its own production before they reach the record, and the headline exact identifications (e3=cos(2pi/9)/864, the D4 ceiling octic) carry genuine multi-route, both-direction verification.
